Supersedes "delivering keys to rented machines is deferred". Jack Heart, 2026-11-14: "if you are doing a very large policy that we don't want to eval on the local machine and ... want to test that against an LLM, then we actually do need both. I think probably we should go ahead and put in the LLM design something for supporting OpenRouter keys. Should be relatively straightforward. I think we've even done it before". Found: Manabot's experiments/jev_mtg183.py and manabot/llm/openrouter.py read OPENROUTER_API_KEY from the process environment and refuse without it; no forwarding to a rental was found there. Etude today gives machines scoped temporary storage grants over the bootstrap link and never the launcher's own keys (docs/launcher.md), and Job.environment values are stored in the job record and its identity. Starting sketch, not accepted: a job names the variables it needs by name only; the launcher reads the values from its own environment when it hands the run down, delivers them with the run's packet, and they never enter job records, identity, logs or artifacts (use the existing sanitizer). A rented marketplace host can read anything on its machine, so recommend a key scoped and spend-capped at the provider for the experiment, which also bounds the per-token cost Etude cannot see.
